sections.title: This week's likely biggest movers
sections.markdown:
The multi-day story turned into a supplier selloff: on Oct 30 the market sold the chip suppliers far harder than the spender, as Amazon recovered most of its after-hours drop while Intel, AMD and the chip ETF slid. This week tests whether that is a "capex peak" fear or a narrower memory-cost squeeze, with the AI hardware chain reporting straight into it: Apple and Palantir (Mon), AMD, Super Micro, Arista and Astera Labs (Tue), Arm, Qualcomm and Coherent (Wed), Lumentum (Thu). The midterms (Tue), Hammack (Thu), Musalem and the jobs report (Fri) keep a December hike in play; oil hinges on Iran's conditional offer to reopen Hormuz. Last week's numbers and the full calendar are in the weekly brief. Each row names the trigger in both directions.

*Updated Sunday, Nov 1 (4:57 p.m. ET) for the week of Nov 2–6. Implied moves are as of Oct 30 and will shift. This is research, not financial advice; I'm not a licensed advisor, and the buy/sell decision is yours.*

| Stock | Sector | Why it should move most | Upside trigger | Downside trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AMD | AI chips | Reports Nov 3 after close (implied ±8.8%, average ±10.6%) after falling \~11% on Intel's PC and memory warning; Helios (MI450) shipments start this quarter and data center is guided to more than double in 2027 | Data center guide and Helios ramp show server share gains while Intel is supply-limited | Client chips hit by memory costs, as Intel flagged; a soft Q4 guide repeats Intel's pattern |
| PLTR | AI software | Nov 2 after close (implied ±12.4%, average ±17%); \~105x forward earnings; needs another sizable full-year raise and U.S. commercial growth well above 100% | A big raise separates AI-outcome software from seat-based SaaS | An in-line guide; a close below \~$186.49 breaks its uptrend |
| SMCI, ANET, ALAB | AI infrastructure (servers, networking) | All Nov 3 after close (implied ±14.4%, ±10.9%, ±15.9%); SMCI already pre-announced $18.5B–$19.5B sales vs. a $14.5B–$15.5B guide | Hyperscalers' bigger 2027 budgets turn into raised guides | Thin margins (SMCI 12–12.5% gross) and "capex peak" talk after Friday's chip slide |
| ARM, QCOM, COHR, LITE, MRVL | AI chips and optics | ARM, QCOM, COHR Nov 4 after close (±15.1%, ±10.6%, ±16.0%); LITE Nov 5 (±13.2%); a Marvell–Lumentum deal could be announced this week | Optics demand confirmed; deal lands at a small premium | Memory costs hit phone and PC volumes (QCOM, ARM royalties); deal dilution weighs on MRVL |
| AAPL | Hardware | Nov 2 after close (implied ±4.2%); first report under CEO John Ternus; last guide was 47–48% gross margin | iPhone strength and margin held despite memory prices | Memory costs dent the margin guide, as Intel warned |
| MU, SKHY | Memory | No report; trade on AMD, SMCI and Apple read-through; memory is the cost that hurt Intel | Buyers confirm memory price rises are sticking | Crowded-trade unwind continues, as on Oct 30 |
| VRT, GEV, ETN | AI infrastructure (power) | Eaton reports Nov 3 before open; read-through from Amazon's "meaningfully more" 2027 capex | Data center orders and backlog confirm the 2027 signal | Hyperscaler cash-burn fear spreads to suppliers |

sections.title: Macro backdrop: a hawkish hold, 5% yields and $100+ oil
sections.markdown:
The Fed held, but two votes for a hike keep a December 9 increase the market's base case, which keeps pressure on high-multiple and debt-funded AI stocks.

**Week of Nov 2:** no Fed meeting, but hike dissenter Beth Hammack speaks Thursday and Alberto Musalem, who said the Fed may need to get back to hiking, speaks Friday after the October jobs report (consensus about +55k, 4.2% unemployment). Futures price roughly 75–85% odds of a December 9 hike; Continuum Economics argues about 50k jobs with steady unemployment keeps it in play. The midterms (Nov 3) and Treasury's refunding (Nov 4) matter for long yields through fiscal policy, not the party result. Data details are in the weekly brief. ([Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/week-in-focus-2nd-6th-november-2026-highlights-include-us-midterm-election-nfp-ism-pmis-rba-boe-and-ez-cpi-), [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/apple-palantir-earnings-october-jobs-report-week-ahead-2026/), [Stocktwits](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/what-to-expect-markets-this-week-nov-1-2026/cNGes4VR923))

**Oct 29 update:** Hot GDP and sticky PCE (figures in the morning brief) leave futures at \~84% odds of a December 9 hike, so long-duration AI names stay the market's funding source until that meeting. ([Barchart via Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stocks-trade-lower-alphabet-disappoints-150533033.html), [StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/stock-market-today-live-october-29-2026), [Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/10/29/stock-market-today-oct-29-marvell-falls-on-lumentum-acquisition-talks/))

- Fed: held at 3.75%–4.00% in a 10–2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook (her first dissent) and Cleveland's Beth Hammack wanted a 25 bp hike. The statement said "the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine" the stance and called uncertainty elevated. Warsh would not commit to December and said he won't decide meetings in advance. Futures price roughly 83–85% odds of a December hike. ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-votes-in-split-decision-to-hold-interest-rates-steady-despite-sticky-inflation-180108960.html), [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/fed-chair-warsh-hesitates-on-december-rate-hike-amid-rising-treasury-yields), [TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours))
- Inflation: September CPI rose 3.7% (core 2.6%), up from 3.4% in August. ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-votes-in-split-decision-to-hold-interest-rates-steady-despite-sticky-inflation-180108960.html))
- Rates: the 10-year rose about 5 bp to \~5.04% during the press conference while the 2-year fell to 4.70%. A steeper curve hurts long-duration growth stocks and debt-funded builders most. ([SRN News](https://srnnews.com/fomc-holds-rates-steady-markets-rise-modestly/))
- Stocks: the S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,743.98 and the chip index (SOX) 1.8%, its fourth straight gain. Utilities and real estate lagged on higher long yields. After hours, QQQ slipped \~0.5% on Alphabet. ([TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours), [RiskReversal](https://riskreversal.substack.com/p/fed-holds-msft-higher-googl-lower))
- Oil: Brent near $111 and WTI near $101. Iran's reply to Qatar's new draft deal is expected by week's end. ([investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/investinglive-european-fx-news-wrap-28-oct/))
- AI financing: Alphabet's free cash flow was negative for a second straight quarter (−$9.1B). It raised $12.4B from share sales and $28.7B in debt during the quarter. ([Cautious Optimism](https://www.cautiousoptimism.news/msft-alpha-earnings), [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/10/28/alphabet-google-stock-drops-cloud-revenue-doubles-free-cash-flow-negative))
- Oct 30 oil-to-rates link: Brent up \~2.5% toward $117 adds to inflation pressure with September core PCE at 3.1%, which supports the \~83% December hike odds. That keeps pressure on long-duration AI names (CRWV, NBIS, ORCL) until Iran resolves. ([TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-oct-30-2026), [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield/news/593653))

sections.title: Options timing: are earnings options cheap or expensive?
sections.markdown:
Last week's scorecard: Alphabet, ServiceNow and Intel moved two to three times what options priced, each on guidance or cash flow; Microsoft, Amazon (by the close), Exxon and Chevron stayed inside. This week, options look rich for MPC, Coherent and Qualcomm and cheap against history for Palantir, AMD, Super Micro and Astera Labs. Buying calls or puts into a report only pays if the stock moves more than options already price in. Implied moves below are as of Oct 30 and will shift.

| Stock | Report | Implied move | Actual, or average move | Last report | Read |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INTC | Oct 29 (done) | ±9.4% | \~−28% close Oct 30 | — | About 3x implied; worst day since the 1970s |
| AMZN | Oct 29 (done) | ±7.6% | −1.4% close Oct 30 (from \~−7% after hours) | — | Inside implied; buyers reversed the after-hours drop |
| GOOGL | Oct 28 (done) | ±6.1% | −12.6% close Oct 29 | — | About 2x implied |
| NOW | Oct 28 (done) | ±10.4% | Down >20% Oct 29 | — | About 2x implied |
| MSFT | Oct 28 (done) | ±4.7%–5.3% | Roughly flat to −2% Oct 29 | — | Inside implied |
| XOM, CVX | Oct 30 (done) | ±3.9% (XOM) | +2.1%, +1.6% | — | Inside implied |
| AAPL | Nov 2, after close | ±4.2% | ±5.0% | −10.0% | Cheaper than its average move |
| PLTR | Nov 2, after close | ±12.4% | ±17.0% | +30.9% | Cheap vs. history; guide decides it |
| MPC | Nov 3, before open | ±10.9% | ±5.2% | +2.6% | Rich: twice its average, priced for an Iran-sized move |
| AMD | Nov 3, after close | ±8.8% | ±10.6% | −7.8% | Slightly cheap; Intel's warning adds risk |
| SMCI | Nov 3, after close | ±14.4% | ±16.0% | +20.7% | Sales pre-announced; margin and guide are the swing |
| ANET | Nov 3, after close | ±10.9% | ±12.0% | +12.8% | Fair to slightly cheap |
| ALAB | Nov 3, after close | ±15.9% | ±17.5% | −12.9% | Fair to slightly cheap |
| DDOG | Nov 4, before open | ±14.3% | ±15.2% | −20.5% | Fair |
| ARM | Nov 4, after close | ±15.1% | ±14.6% | +19.4% | Fair |
| QCOM | Nov 4, after close | ±10.6% | ±7.5% | −6.2% | Rich vs. its average |
| COHR | Nov 4, after close | ±16.0% | ±8.0% | −8.5% | Rich: twice its average |
| LITE | Nov 5, after close | ±13.2% | ±11.3% | +17.8% | Slightly rich; deal news could land first |
| NVDA | Late Nov. (unconfirmed) | Not priced yet (last ±5.9%) | ±4.0% | — | Options have overpriced the closing move 4 of the last 5 times |

**What this means for timing:**

1. When a report changes the cash-flow or guidance story, history understates the move: Alphabet, ServiceNow and Intel all beat on headline numbers and still fell two to three times their implied moves. History is a base rate, not a forecast.
2. After hours is not the close. Amazon's \~−7% after hours became −1.4% at the close, while Alphabet's drop widened overnight. Averages above use closing moves.
3. Rich options (MPC, COHR, QCOM): buying calls or puts outright needs an outsized surprise; debit spreads cut the cost.
4. Cheaper options (PLTR, AMD, SMCI, ALAB): moves have tended to beat the implied move, but Friday's chip slide already reset prices, so part of the bad news may be in.
5. Read-through stocks (MU, SKHY, NVDA, AVGO, MRVL, VRT) have no earnings premium of their own to collapse, so Tuesday's AMD, Super Micro, Arista and Astera Labs reports reprice them overnight.
6. Expiries: the first weekly after a report (Nov 6 for this week's reporters) is cheapest but takes the full crush, and Friday's jobs report lands on that same expiry. One more week adds cushion.

Past moves don't predict the next one. Sources: [EarningsWatcher MSFT](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/msft-earnings-october-2026), [EarningsWatcher GOOGL](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/googl-earnings-october-2026), [EarningsWatcher AMZN](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/amzn-implied-move), [EarningsWatcher AMZN options](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/amzn-earnings-options), [EarningsWatcher INTC](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/intc-earnings-october-2026), [EarningsWatcher AAPL](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/aapl-implied-move), [EarningsWatcher PLTR](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/pltr-earnings-november-2026), [EarningsWatcher AMD](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/amd-earnings-november-2026), [Q3 implied vs. actual tracker](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/q3-2026-implied-vs-actual-tracker), [ZeroHedge (MSFT after hours)](https://zerohedge.com/markets/msft-rises-azure-beat-bookings-shrink-and-backlog-stalls), [RiskReversal](https://riskreversal.substack.com/p/fed-holds-msft-higher-googl-lower), [Investing.com (GOOGL)](https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/earnings-call-transcript-alphabet-q3-2026-profit-miss-sparks-10-afterhours-drop-93CH-5662008), [PANews (NOW)](https://panews.io/articles/01a1844b-23c0-762e-84fc-a5ee2a94208b), [TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours).

sections.title: AI cloud
sections.markdown:
Amazon confirmed the pattern: the market pays for cloud growth but sells negative free cash flow. AWS grew 39%, its fastest in nearly five years, yet the stock fell \~7% after hours because trailing free cash flow hit −$42.4B and 2027 capex goes higher still. Alphabet closed down 12.6% on the same worry.

| Company | Result or setup | Versus the bar | Read |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Amazon (AMZN), Q3 2026](https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Third-Quarter-Results/default.aspx) | Revenue $201.9B (+12%) vs. \~$202.2B; EPS $1.89 vs. \~$1.97; AWS $46.0B (+39%), 38.7% margin; record 13.9% company operating margin | Backlog $578B; Q3 capex $77.3B; 2026 held at \~$220B, 2027 "meaningfully more"; trailing free cash flow −$42.4B; Q4 sales guide $240B–$247B | Down \~7% after hours (implied ±7.6%); AWS seen growing >40% in 2027 and 2028 |
| [Microsoft (MSFT)](https://phemex.com/news/article/microsoft-q1-fy2027-revenue-hits-923b-as-azure-grows-48-yoy-101615), fiscal Q1 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) | Azure +48% cc vs. 44–45% guide (headline results in the Oct 29 morning brief) | Capex incl. leases $45.2B vs. \~$50B+ expected; commercial bookings −12%; RPO flat at $677B; FQ2 Azure guide reported at \~49% | Up 2–6% after hours, then roughly flat to −2% on Oct 29 |
| [Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://fortune.com/2026/10/28/alphabet-google-stock-drops-cloud-revenue-doubles-free-cash-flow-negative), Q3 2026 | Cloud $30.7B (+103%), 36.2% margin (headline results in the Oct 29 morning brief) | Backlog $561B (from $514B); capex $51.4B; 2026 guide held at $195B–$205B; 2027 to "rise significantly"; free cash flow −$9.1B | Closed −12.6% Oct 29, about $500B of market value |
| Meta (META, reported Oct 21) | Revenue +26% to $64.6B; free cash flow −$2.1B | 2026 capex now $135B–$145B | New non-voting class to fund AI shows how capital-hungry this is |
| Oracle, CoreWeave, Nebius | ORCL +10.7% Oct 28 on investor day: >35% yearly revenue growth FY26–FY30, ≥$225B FY30 revenue; CRWV +7.3%, NBIS +7.0% | Funding costs with the 10-year near 5%; CRWV bonds near 15% | The leveraged tail; moves 2–3x the hyperscalers on any news |

**Most likely to move (week of Nov 2):** CoreWeave, into its Nov 10 report (the same morning as October CPI), with Nebius and Oracle alongside. No hyperscaler reports this week, so cloud names trade on two things: whether AMD, Super Micro and Arista confirm the 2027 build is still accelerating, which supports neocloud order books, and whether the jobs report and Fed speakers lift long yields, the neoclouds' funding cost. Amazon's near-flat close on Oct 30 after a \~7% after-hours drop hints the cash-burn selling in the spenders is fading; Alphabet's follow-through is the test. ([Earnings Whispers (CRWV)](https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/CRWV), [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm))

**Second-order effect:** Alphabet said TPU system sales were a meaningful part of Cloud growth and expects a bigger ramp in 2027, making Google a chip seller as well as a cloud. OpenAI and Oracle are reported to be using Google's chips. **Disclosure:** Anthropic, the company that makes me, is a large Google TPU customer, so weigh my framing here.

**Amazon second-order effects:** Trainium and Graviton revenue commitments each rose more than 20x, most Bedrock workloads run on Trainium, and Amazon plans to sell Trainium to outside customers starting late 2027. That makes Amazon, like Google, a chip seller as well as a cloud, a long-run threat to Nvidia's share and a tailwind for memory makers. **Disclosure:** Amazon is a major investor in Anthropic, the company that makes me, and Anthropic is a large AWS and Trainium customer; Amazon's EPS decline was partly a tough comparison with Anthropic investment gains a year ago. Weigh my framing here accordingly.

sections.title: AI infrastructure: power and cooling
sections.markdown:
The "picks and shovels" suppliers both reported blowout quarters this morning. They are the cleanest read on what hyperscaler capex turns into.

| Company | Q3 2026 result | What it tells us |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vertiv (VRT) | Sales $4.31B (+61%) vs. \~$3.75B expected; adj. EPS $2.21 vs. $1.82; organic orders up over 100%; raised full-year guidance | Power and cooling demand is accelerating, not peaking; stock was up \~4% early today |

sections.title: AI chips and memory
sections.markdown:
Amazon is the new demand signal: Q3 capex of $77.3B, 2027 "meaningfully more," and Trainium commitments up more than 20x. Intel added a second one: memory costs are now squeezing chip buyers, which is pricing power for memory makers. Chips still fell on Oct 29 (semiconductor ETF down \~2%, Micron and Arm down 3%+, Broadcom −1.9%, Nvidia −0.8%) as Alphabet's drop and weak Korean memory results weighed. ([Barchart via Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stocks-trade-lower-alphabet-disappoints-150533033.html), [Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/10/29/stock-market-today-oct-29-marvell-falls-on-lumentum-acquisition-talks/))

| Company | Latest data point | Why it moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Intel (INTC)](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/intel-q3-2026-slides-record-data-center-growth-stock-tumbles-on-outlook-93CH-4985517) | Q3 revenue $16.5B (+21%); data center $7.3B (+78%); foundry loss $1.9B (margin −27.7% from −36.2%), outside foundry revenue $411M; Q4 guide $15B–$16B at 38% margin; down \~17–21% after hours | Data center strength is real, but memory costs, a Fab 28 shutdown (\~$300M, \~200 bp of margin), supply limits into H1 2027 and no positive free cash flow in 2027 dominate |
| Micron (MU) | Says 2027 HBM is largely sold out at "much higher" prices; DRAM prices rose high-teens % last quarter, NAND \~30%; down 3%+ Oct 29 | Amazon's 2027 capex raise and Intel's memory-cost warning both point to more pricing power |
| SK Hynix (SKHY, Nasdaq ADR) | Record Q3; says DRAM and HBM sold out through 2029; up \~13% on Oct 28 | Same thesis; TrendForce sees DRAM contract prices up another 10–15% in Q4 |
| Marvell (MRVL) | Fell 13.2% to $218.34 on Oct 29 on reported advanced talks to buy Lumentum (LITE) in an all-stock deal; an announcement could come next week | Dilution and integration risk vs. owning more of the AI optics chain; also a custom-chip supplier to Amazon |
| Broadcom (AVGO) | Banks lining up a \~$63B financing to build AI compute (with Apollo, Blackstone); −1.9% Oct 29 | Custom chips for AI labs, including Google's TPUs; Alphabet says TPU system sales ramp into 2027 |
| TSMC (TSM) | Q3 revenue $46.7B, above the top of guidance; net income +68.7% | Makes Trainium, TPUs and Nvidia GPUs alike, so every capex raise lands here; margin dilution from 2 nm and U.S. fabs is the drag |
| AMD | Reports Nov 3; guided $12.7B–$13.3B; implied ±8.9% | Intel's supply limits are a server share opportunity; Intel's PC warning is a risk to AMD's client unit |
| Nvidia (NVDA) | Reports late Nov. (unconfirmed); −0.8% Oct 29 | Amazon and Google now both sell their own AI chips; Nvidia's report is the AI-cycle verdict |

**Most likely to move (week of Nov 2):** AMD on Nov 3 (implied ±8.8%), after an \~11% drop on Oct 30 in sympathy with Intel. The test is whether data center growth (guided to more than double in 2027) and the Helios ramp outweigh memory-cost pressure on its PC chips. OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic are its named anchor customers; Anthropic makes me, so weigh my framing. Then Arm, Qualcomm and Coherent (Nov 4), Lumentum (Nov 5) and Marvell on possible deal news. Micron and SK Hynix have no report but reprice on each; Nvidia's own verdict comes in late November. ([Hudson Labs](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/amd-q3-2026-earnings-preview-revenue-guidance-key-drivers), [Yahoo (Marvell–Lumentum)](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/nvidia-backed-marvell-lumentum-could-191329102.html))

**Risk:** Memory was the most crowded trade in the October selloff. SK Hynix fell 9.6% in one session during that slide, so the downside is just as sharp.

**Disclosure:** Some Broadcom financing reporting ties these deals to Anthropic, the company that makes me. I note it so you can weigh my framing.

sections.title: AI software
sections.markdown:
ServiceNow's after-hours drop shows the AI-disruption trade against seat-based software is not over, even when growth and AI bookings beat. Companies selling AI outcomes still rerate up; legacy SaaS trades on fear that AI agents replace it.

| Company | Setup | Why it moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Palantir (PLTR) | Reports Nov 2; est. $0.36 EPS, $2.00B revenue; beat 5 straight quarters | Highest-multiple AI software name; guidance decides the reaction |
| ServiceNow (NOW) | Q3 subscription revenue $3.99B (+21%, +20.5% cc) vs. \~20% guide; AI contract-value target raised to $1.7B from $1B; Q4 guide below the Street; fell more than 20% on Oct 29 | Disruption fear won again despite beats on growth and AI |
| Microsoft (MSFT) | Copilot adoption and its own models, alongside Azure | The software side of tonight's report |
**Most likely to move (week of Nov 2):** Palantir on Nov 2 (implied ±12.4%, average ±17%). At \~105x forward earnings it needs another sizable full-year raise and U.S. commercial growth well above 100%; an in-line guide risks breaking its uptrend near $186.49. Datadog (Nov 4, before open, ±14.3%) and Cloudflare (Nov 5) test AI-native usage demand; Atlassian and HubSpot test whether seat-based software keeps derating after ServiceNow. ([TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262260538-palantir-stock-forecast-q3-earnings-preview-guidance-raise-186-support-october-31-2026-tradingkey), [Earnings Watcher](https://earnings-watcher.com/earnings-this-week))

**Sector event:** Anthropic has filed an S-1 to list on Nasdaq; Bloomberg reported the roadshow could begin as soon as the week of Nov 9, with trading before Thanksgiving (not confirmed). A large AI listing can pull money from existing AI software stocks, or reprice them higher as a comparison point. ([Implicator](https://www.implicator.ai/anthropic-could-start-ipo-roadshow-week-of-nov-9-putting-debut-before-thanksgiving/))

**Disclosure:** I'm built by Anthropic, so I'm not a neutral source on that IPO. I won't give a view on it; treat it purely as a sector catalyst.

Sources: [Benzinga (PLTR)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PLTR/earnings), [Earnings Whispers (PLTR drift)](https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/PLTR), [XTB (NOW)](https://www.xtb.com/cy/market-analysis/news-and-research/servicenow-shares-jump-7-after-earnings-is-the-software-sector-poised-for-a-rebound), [TIKR (NOW)](https://www.tikr.com/blog/servicenow-jumped-7-on-a-150-analyst-target-heres-where-the-stock-could-go), [Yahoo market wrap](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-news-oct-28-081900420.html).

sections.title: Oil and gas
sections.markdown:
Exxon and Chevron beat on refining, not crude, and both stocks rose only about 2% premarket, inside implied moves. The next 1–2 weeks still hinge on Iran, and refiners and E&Ps carry the most exposure in both directions. Headline numbers are in the Oct 30 morning brief.

| Company | Latest data point | Why it moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valero (VLO), Marathon (MPC), Phillips 66 (PSX) | Fell 7–9% on Oct 27 when fuel prices dropped faster than crude after Trump's "plummeting" post and talk of a Russian-diesel waiver. XOM ran U.S. Gulf Coast refineries at 100% and CVX at \~98% | Most leveraged to crack spreads, both ways; MPC reports Nov 3 |
| Exxon (XOM) | Refining (Energy Products) out-earned upstream; production 4,496 koebd, slightly down q/q; $20B buyback planned for 2027 | Buybacks and debt cuts cushion a price drop; +2.1% premarket vs. ±3.9% implied |
| Chevron (CVX) | Adj. EPS $5.28 vs. $4.78 est.; downstream $3.58B vs. $638M a year ago; capex fell as Permian spending eased | Same cushion as XOM; trades on the Q4 margin outlook |
| E&Ps (COP, OXY, EOG) | Brent \~$117 and WTI \~$104 Friday morning after Hormuz mine claims | Purest crude exposure with no refining offset; biggest movers on Iran headlines |
| SLB, HAL, BKR | Majors are cutting Permian spending and returning cash instead | Services lag the oil price; HAL is most tied to U.S. land drilling |

**Most likely to move (week of Nov 2):** Marathon Petroleum on Nov 3 before the open (implied ±10.9%, twice its average move), with Valero alongside, then ConocoPhillips (Nov 5) and EOG (Nov 5, after close). Over the weekend Iran called Vance's outreach "a positive step" and, with Qatari mediators, offered to reopen Hormuz in two days instead of seven, but only if sanctions and oil waivers are restored, U.S. forces cut and frozen funds released. The IRGC said four tankers burned on Oct 30, and Trump says the war will end "very soon." Brent settled near $113 on Friday. BP's warning that refining margins are softening keeps refiners the most two-way. ([HNGN](https://www.hngn.com/articles/273637/20261031/qatar-carries-revised-deal-tehran-trump-sees-war-ending.htm), [Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/week-in-focus-2nd-6th-november-2026-highlights-include-us-midterm-election-nfp-ism-pmis-rba-boe-and-ez-cpi-), [Earnings Watcher](https://earnings-watcher.com/earnings-this-week))

**Both directions:** Upside if Iran's conditions stall talks past the midterms or tanker attacks continue and Brent holds above \~$110: refiners and E&Ps extend. Downside if Washington accepts a version of the two-day reopening: refiners fall first and hardest, as on Oct 27, then E\&Ps; XOM and CVX lose least.

Sources: [Oilprice (Valero)](https://oilprice.com/Company-News/Valero-Q3-Earnings-Surge-Sixfold-to-68-Billion-on-Refining-Boom.amp.html), [247 Wall St (Valero)](https://247wallst.com/cards/valero-energy-q3-2026-earnings-vlo-01m5hs2e7dnht5h4w2ey4hf68p), [Pluang (Exxon, Trump)](https://pluang.com/en/news-feed/trump-perkirakan-perang-iran-berakhir-harga-minyak-turun-setelah-pemilu), [SLB release](https://www.sttinfo.fi/tiedote/72439583/slb-announces-third-quarter-2026-results?publisherId=58763726), [AInvest (EIA)](https://www.ainvest.com/news/iran-oil-windfall-priced-eia-won-2608/), [investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/investinglive-european-fx-news-wrap-28-oct/), [Yahoo live blog](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-october-28-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-fed-meeting-decision-big-tech-earnings-130508769.html).

sections.title: Scenarios: what would change the picture
sections.markdown:
| If this happens | Rough odds, next 2 weeks | Likely winners | Likely losers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hyperscalers raise capex and cloud growth accelerates | 60% (this week's test: AMD, SMCI, ANET, ALAB guides) | MU, SKHY, VRT, GEV, AVGO, CRWV | Hyperscaler stocks themselves if cash flow weakens |
| Capex rises but cloud growth slows | 15% (no hyperscaler reports until 2027 guides) | Suppliers short-term | GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN (repeat of Alphabet's July drop) |
| Fed signals a December hike | 55% (Hammack Nov 5, jobs and Musalem Nov 6, CPI Nov 10) | Banks, cash | CRWV, NBIS, ORCL, high-multiple software |
| Fed sounds patient, yields ease below 5% | 30% (needs a soft jobs report and CPI) | Leveraged AI builders, small caps | — |
| Iran deal reached | 30% (two-day Hormuz offer is on the table, with conditions) | Airlines, consumers | VLO, MPC, PSX hardest; COP, OXY next; XOM, CVX least |
| Iran talks collapse | 25% (tanker attacks continue; strikes not ruled out) | VLO, XOM, CVX | Rate-sensitive tech (oil feeds inflation, inflation feeds hikes) |
| Memory costs squeeze chip buyers | 50% (new row; tested by AMD, AAPL, QCOM guides) | MU, SKHY | AMD client, AAPL margins, QCOM, PC makers |

Odds are my rough judgment for the next two weeks, not market-implied, and rows can overlap. Live now: the first row for suppliers versus spenders, and the new memory-cost row Intel opened on Oct 29. The hike row is the one that would hurt the AI builders most, and it gets three tests before Nov 10.
